text.title: Freelancer Inbound Reply Template Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on who sent the inbound, which of scope, budget and deadline it already states, and where the reply will be read, to the rule that constrains the reply being drafted.

decision-tree.root-question: Is this a first touch from someone who is not already a client, about work the operator actually does?

branch.when: the sender is an existing client, or it is a mass recruiter message naming a stack the operator does not work in

conclusion.verdict: skip; reply in the existing project channel, or decline — a qualifier to a current client re-opens a settled scope and a trust signal spent on a blast message is wasted

branch.when: cold or warm first touch in the operator's line of work
branch.question: Which of scope, budget and deadline does the message already state?

branch.when: none of the three; it is a two-line 'are you available' with nothing to work from
branch.question: Will the reply be triaged as a two-line preview — LinkedIn inbox, mobile mail notification — before anyone opens it?

branch.when: yes; the decision to open happens on the preview

conclusion.verdict: place the qualifier after the acknowledgement and before any background, and hold the whole reply at or under about 120 words

branch.when: no; a threaded email the sender will open in full

conclusion.verdict: ask for exactly one of scope, budget or deadline; one question mark in the whole reply, so it stays answerable in the same sitting

branch.when: scope is described but no budget is named
branch.question: Is the sender asking for a rate or a ballpark figure in this first message?

branch.when: yes, a number is requested while scope is still a paragraph of intent

conclusion.verdict: no rate, total or range in this reply; qualify scope first, or every later detail reads to the client as a price rise from your first figure

branch.when: no; scope is concrete enough to propose the next move

conclusion.verdict: propose one action carrying two named slots with a timezone, or one specific async question — never 'let me know what works'

branch.when: budget and deadline are stated; what is missing is a reason to trust the operator
branch.question: Is there an openable link, a nameable prior client, or a measured result with unit and period available right now?

branch.when: yes; a resolvable artefact exists and may be cited

conclusion.verdict: cite that artefact as the trust signal; years of experience and stack lists carry no discriminating information in that inbox

branch.when: no; only years of experience and a stack list are available

conclusion.verdict: lead with a concrete noun lifted from the inbound — product, stack, company, named deadline — since proving the message was read is the only discriminator left

branch.when: the inbound is a full brief with scope, budget and deadline all stated

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; draft all four lines and check them against the rule set before sending
